 ATR Urges House to Pass The Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act
 Mike Palicz and Rachel Loren 
 11/20/2026
 Share 
 Twitter 
 Facebook 
 LinkedIn 
 Americans for Tax Reform urges the House to pass the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act ( S. 5441 ), a pro-taxpayer package of  65 reforms  aimed at improving Internal Revenue Service (IRS) operations and taxpayer services. The legislation cleared the Senate in September with unanimous support.
 The legislation, led by Senate Finance Chair Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) and Ranking member Ron Wyden (D-Oregon), would make the IRS more responsive and accountable to taxpayers. 
 Key reforms include:
 1. Digitization of Tax Returns and Correspondence 
 The legislation would modernize the IRS’ processing systems by requiring the agency to accept and process returns electronically and digitize paper returns and correspondence. Currently, the IRS relies on manual processing and can even print digital submissions and process them by hand. This provision would reduce the unnecessary administrative burden that contributes to backlogs and delays. 
 2. Creation of Dashboard with Individualized Taxpayer Information 
 This legislation helps to limit the number of unnecessary calls and letters sent to the IRS by requiring the IRS to provide a user-friendly and real-time information dashboard that will inform taxpayers to updates on call volume, processing delays, wait times, and callback availability. The bill also requires the IRS to issue weekly delay disclosures and, as a result, manage taxpayer expectations and reduce calls. 
 The dashboard will enable taxpayers to access more individualized information regarding the status of their returns or refunds, including possible delays and any additional documentation or information required by the IRS to process their return. 
 3. Stronger Protections Against Improper Tax Return Preparers  
 The bill closes a loophole in current law that allows tax preparers to avoid penalties if they alter a taxpayer’s signed return, including changing refund destinations. Instead, the legislation would allow preparer penalties to apply where willful violations involving preparer tax identification numbers (PTINs), including fines and jail time. The bill requires real-time validation of Electronic Filing Identification Numbers (EFINs) which will help to prevent the use of suspended, revoked, expired, or compromised credentials.
 4.   Tax Court Procedure Overhauls 
 The legislation makes a series of changes that will make Tax Court proceedings more accessible and give taxpayers more opportunities to challenge IRS decisions. The legislation authorizes the Tax Court to issue third-party subpoenas for testimony and document production before the hearing which will decrease the likelihood of cases, which would otherwise be settled, that go to trial. It also clarifies when filing deadlines can be extended and give the court more flexibility in correcting certain mistakes.
 The section of the bill also provides that Special Trial Judges are authorized to share the workload of the Tax Court, which can increase the productivity and efficiency of the Tax Court. Further, the bill would raise the “small tax case” threshold from $50,000 to $100,000 and indexed for inflation. These cases use simpler evidentiary rules and are generally resolved more quickly than other Tax Court proceedings.
 5. Expanded Taxpayer Appeal Rights 
 The bill strengthens taxpayers’ ability to challenge IRS decisions without immediately going to Tax Court. Through this bill the IRS would be required to timely review refund claims and issue a written determination within 12 months. If a refund claim is denied, the IRS must explain its decision and tell the taxpayer how to appeal it through the Office of Appeals. 
 Americans for Tax Reform supports the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act and urges the House to pass these pro-taxpayer reforms so taxpayers receive faster service, stronger protections, better access, and clearer information from the IRS.
